note: Seed questions for login prompts. kind: text | choice | scale (1 to 5; options = [low label, high label]). bank_key must be unique and never change once shipped.

questions.text: Which sentence sounds most like you?
options: I think most teams overcomplicate this.
Honestly, most teams make this harder than it needs to be.
In my view, many teams introduce unnecessary complexity.
Here's the thing: it's simpler than people make it.

questions.text: How formal should your writing feel?
Do you prefer to write in the first person?
How much humor belongs in your posts?
options: A dry line now and then

questions.text: Do you use contractions (don't, it's, can't) when you write?
Name a writer, blog or publication whose tone you'd like to borrow from. What do you like about it?
Are there words or phrases you use a lot and want kept in your writing?
Which words or phrases make you wince when you see them in writing?
What sentence length reads most natural to you?
How strongly should your opinions come through?
Who is the one reader you picture while you write?
How much do your readers already know about your topics?
What do you most want a reader to do or think differently after reading your posts?
How do you want to handle technical terms?
Is there a region or community your readers mostly belong to? Should the writing reflect it?
What kind of sections do you like to read?
How do you like a post to open?
options: With the main point straight away

questions.text: How should a post end?
options: Stop when the point is made

questions.text: How do you feel about bullet lists in a blog post?
What length do you prefer for a typical post?
What style of headings do you prefer?
How much should your claims lean on named sources versus your own experience?
Which kinds of sources do you trust most? (for example journals, government reports, trade press, books)
Any sources, authors or sites you want tea to avoid?
How do you feel about statistics in a post?
When the evidence is unclear, how should the post handle it?
options: Present the strongest view and note the doubt

questions.text: How visible should citations be in the text?
options: A sources list at the end

questions.text: What is one thing you learned recently that you'd like to write about?
What is a mistake you made recently that taught you something?
What do people usually get wrong about the subjects you care about?
If a friend asked about one of your topics over coffee, what would you tell them?
What's a concrete example from your own work or study that you often come back to?
What's something you used to believe about your field that you've changed your mind on?
What's something you've built, written or done lately that you're proud of, and why?
What advice do you wish someone had given you a year ago?
Is there anything you can't or don't want to mention in your posts? (employers, clients, unpublished work, people)
How should tea handle real people or organizations in a post?
options: Name only public figures and organizations

questions.text: How do you want to handle politically charged topics?
options: Take a clear position when I choose to

questions.text: How personal should your posts get?
